newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla to pasteurize apple juice products.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla to pasteurize apple juice products.

text.p: Odwalla Inc said its executives have decided to remarket their apple juice based products using juice that has been "flash pasteurized," and could return products to store shelves by this weekend.

An Odwalla spokeswoman confirmed the company's management had taken the decision, in consultation with a scientific advisory panel it had formed after an outbreak of E. coli bacterial disease linked to its apple juice-based drinks. More than 50 people in several western states and Canada had been sickened by the bacterial outbreak, including one young child who died last month.

Odwalla voluntarily withdrew all its apple juice and apple juice-based products after the outbreak was linked to its juices and it called for all other producers to stop selling unpasteurized apple juice until the industry could ensure the safety of the product.
The company has been cooperating with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to try to trace the cause of the contamination, but an inspection of Odwalla's plant in Dinuba, California found no E.coli.
Sydney Fisher, director of communicatioins at Odwalla, said the product will be on store shelves in California starting today and throughout its seven state region beginning Friday.

"Ever since this happened we've been considering all of the options available to us and we found flash pasteurization was a process that guarantees safety and still preserves the vibrant flavor and traditional value of the juice," he said.
Odwalla is re-introducing 12 of the product it had pulled from the shelves, but is still studying how it can process and bring three carrot-juice based products back on the market.
Shares of Odwalla were off 7/8 at 13-1/4 in late trading on the Nasdaq market.
